Definition: Integration of farmer registries, agricultural input vouchers, land registrations, extension services data
Comments: No evidence found on agriculture system integration with data exchange.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A single fast-path search on agricultural digitisation in Equatorial Guinea surfaced no sector-specific source, but batch-level evidence gathered for other rows in this country (World Bank 2023/24 Digital Economy Diagnostic, fetched and read; GITGE institutional study reported 2 July 2026) is directly relevant and shows no national data exchange or interoperability platform exists in Equatorial Guinea at all — ministries digitise in silos and cross-agency interoperability was measured at only 15% (GITGE, June 2026). revised_comments: Equatorial Guinea has no operational government data exchange or interoperability platform, so agriculture-sector data (farmer registries, input vouchers, land records, extension services) cannot be integrated into any cross-government system. A World Bank digital economy diagnostic found ministries digitising services in silos with no shared data layer, and a June 2026 GITGE institutional study measured cross-agency interoperability at just 15%, confirming the continued absence of integration.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government data exchange systems. 25 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Level of public transparency regarding data exchange operations, governance, and data sharing agreements
Comments: No documented transparency mechanisms for government data exchange operations. Freedom House score of 5/100 (2021). No public dashboard or reporting on digital government data systems.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Both originally cited sources fetched and read. dataprotection.africa confirms Equatorial Guinea has a data protection law but had not appointed a Data Protection Authority as at its last update (24 June 2022); it does not mention a Freedom House score, and the World Bank diagnostic does not either — the 'Freedom House score of 5/100 (2021)' figure in the original comments could not be verified against either cited source. Substantively, since no government data exchange or interoperability platform exists at all (World Bank 2023/24 diagnostic; GITGE institutional study, June 2026, interoperability at 15%), there are no data exchange operations, governance arrangements or data-sharing agreements for the public to be transparent about. Code confirmed at 0, now on the basis of a genuinely n.a. situation (no data exchange object exists) rather than unresearched Unknown; left unchanged as no positive transparency mechanism exists to warrant 1-4.
revised_comments: No public transparency mechanisms exist for government data exchange operations in Equatorial Guinea, because no operational data exchange or interoperability platform exists in the first place. Government digitisation proceeds ministry by ministry in silos, with no shared governance framework, public dashboard or reporting on cross-agency data sharing; a June 2026 GITGE institutional study measured cross-agency interoperability at only 15%. Equatorial Guinea has enacted a data protection law but has not yet appointed a Data Protection Authority.
